source: Quiz 2 - Sessions 1-3: Choosing a Model and Thinking Budgets
question: When you move from a larger Claude tier down to a smaller one, what largely carries over with you?

options.text: Most of the tooling the larger tier had
options.feedback: Size mostly buys knowledge and reasoning, not access. The smaller tier still reaches the same kinds of tools, which is why dropping a tier usually costs less than students expect.

options.text: Most of the world knowledge the larger tier had
options.feedback: World knowledge is one of the two things named as lost when you go smaller. A smaller model holds the world in fewer numbers, so the gaps show up here first.

options.text: Most of the reasoning quality on hard problems
options.feedback: Reasoning quality is usually the other casualty of going smaller. Some tasks will not survive the drop, which is why you test rather than assume.

options.text: Most of the wording of the answers it gave
options.feedback: Different tiers are different models, so they will not phrase things the same way even on an easy task. What carries across is the surrounding tooling, not the text.
